page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-8GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis, 2 physical cores, and 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tiers for compute-intensive tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both fall into the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers, with scores of 780.18 and 1543.28 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance in the bottom 25%, with read-only large block speeds at 27.8 GB/sec and write speeds at 25.1 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations like gzip compression at 24.0 GB/sec and Geekbench single-core tests at 1934.0 achieve average tier results.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation, which limits its sustained multi-core throughput, as evidenced by a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 3268.0 and a poor static web serving throughput of 2.27 GB/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared-resource model offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that do not require continuous high-performance compute resources, making it a viable option for lightweight utility tasks.

This server is best suited for low-traffic web serving, basic text processing, lightweight single-threaded applications, and development or testing environments that do not demand sustained multi-core CPU performance.
